observation.visible_scene: Two parallel descending staircases built from block steps sit on a glossy black surface: the left flight has teal treads with yellow risers, the right flight has magenta treads with yellow risers. Each staircase is topped by a single upright picture-card domino, backed by a row of gray blocks. A horizontal row of standing white dominoes lies at the upper-left edge and another at the lower-right edge; a black frame caps the bottom of each staircase. A 'FlippyCat' watermark is fixed at the top-left. The glossy floor shows faint mirrored reflections of the steps.
visible_changes: For roughly the first half of the excerpt (frames 1-16) the scene is essentially static: both picture cards stand upright at the tops of their staircases and the white domino rows remain standing.

From about frame 17 onward the two picture cards tip over and begin tumbling down their respective staircases, descending step by step (appearing motion-blurred and changing orientation as they roll) and continuing to move downward through the final frame.
The right card and left card progress down their own flights in parallel, each staying on its own staircase; neither crosses to the other.
The camera viewpoint, the gray backing blocks, the black end-frames, and both white domino rows (upper-left and lower-right) stay fixed and unchanged throughout the clip.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiated the cards toppling is not shown; no contact, push, or chain reaction from the white domino rows is visible within the excerpt.
The cards' final resting positions and whether they reach the bottom barriers are beyond the clip's end.
Whether the standing white domino rows are part of a larger sequence that started before this segment is unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact frame of toppling onset is approximate (cards are upright through frame 16 and clearly falling by frame 17-18).
Heavy motion blur makes the cards' printed faces and colors hard to track frame-to-frame, so individual color readings are uncertain.
The upper-left white domino row's sawtooth appearance is a side view of standing pieces; subtle tilt there cannot be confirmed as motion versus viewing angle.
